items.impact: Deafblind users reading with a braille display, who can use neither captions nor audio description, and blind users who prefer text, miss any visual information. A descriptive transcript is the only format that serves them.
items.problem: The page offers an audio-described video, so there is visual content worth describing, but the transcript holds only speech: no descriptions of slides, charts, on-screen text or who is shown.

items.fix: Add a chapters track (for example "Introduction", "Dr Okafor's opening", "Professor Lindqvist's reply", "Discussion", "Chair's close"), a visible chapter list with timestamps as buttons that seek the video, and timestamp links in the transcript. Test seeking by keyboard, switch and screen reader.
items.impact: Keyboard and switch users and people with tremor find fine seeking slow or impossible; screen-reader users hear the slider only as a time value; people with cognitive or memory impairments cannot easily return to a point or follow structure. Finding one argument in nearly an hour is very hard.
items.problem: The 58-minute recording has no kind="chapters" track, no timestamped table of contents, and no transcript links that move the video. The only way to find a section is the native seek slider.

items.fix: Add aria-labelledby pointing at the <h1> (give it an id), or add aria-label="Debate recording: should the four-day school week be scrapped?".
items.impact: Screen-reader users are not told which recording the player holds or that it is the main content, especially on pages or in element lists with more than one media item.
items.problem: The <video> has no aria-label or aria-labelledby. Screen readers announce only "video" or "media", and the poster image has no text alternative.

items.fix: Show the transcript expanded by default (<details open>) or as an ordinary section under its own heading. Test find-in-page and reading extensions in Chrome, Firefox and Safari.
items.impact: People with cognitive, memory or reading disabilities who use Ctrl+F, and users of translation, reader-mode or text-to-speech extensions, searching for "childcare" or "secondary" find nothing or only the incorrect AI summary, worsening the steering problem in F4.
items.problem: When the transcript is collapsed its text is not rendered. Browsers that do not auto-open <details> for find-in-page matches will not find words in it, and some reader and translation tools skip collapsed content.
